meta.title: EmuLabZip – Android Emulator & iOS Simulator Debugging Lab
meta.description: EmuLabZip is a free, open-source lab to inspect, monitor and debug apps in Android emulators and iOS simulators: logs, network, performance, crashes and more.
meta.ogAlt: EmuLabZip showing the overview of an Android emulator in a dark, futuristic interface

hero.lead: EmuLabZip brings logs, network traffic, performance, memory, storage, crashes and accessibility of your Android emulators and iOS simulators into one fast, native app. Nothing to install on the device.
hero.shotAlt: EmuLabZip desktop app showing the overview of an Android emulator: build, hardware, display, battery and a live screen preview

features.title: One lab for everything your emulator knows
features.lead: Stop switching between Logcat, Instruments, Android Studio profilers and a proxy. EmuLabZip reads the public interfaces of the platforms, so it keeps working when Xcode and Android Studio update.

items.title: Live logs
items.text: logcat and the iOS unified log in one table that stays smooth at thousands of lines per second, with level, tag, text and regex filters.

items.title: Performance
items.text: CPU, memory, frame rate, janky frames and battery for the app you pick, charted as it runs.

items.title: Memory
items.text: Snapshots with a diff by category, plus heap dumps (.hprof) and memory graphs (.memgraph) one click away.

items.title: Storage
items.text: Browse an app's sandbox and open SQLite databases, preferences, property lists, JSON and images in place.

items.title: Network proxy
items.text: Decrypt HTTPS from your app, read headers and bodies, follow WebSockets and HTTP/3, export HAR, import packet captures.

items.title: Mocks and breakpoints
items.text: Answer a request yourself, slow it down, block it, or stop it and edit the request or the response.

items.title: Traces and flame graphs
items.text: Perfetto system traces with SQL, simpleperf and Instruments recordings, shown as flame graphs.

items.title: Crashes and ANRs
items.text: Crashes, native crashes and ANRs with stacks, the facts the device wrote down and hints for symbolication.

items.title: Device controls
items.text: Change location, dark mode, the status bar, battery, permissions, notifications and links, each with a way back.

items.title: Layout and accessibility
items.text: See every view of a screen and audit labels, touch targets and contrast, on Android and the iOS Simulator.

items.title: Sessions and CI
items.text: Record a whole run into one file, and let emulabzip ci record around your test command in GitHub Actions.

items.title: Compare devices
items.text: Two emulators side by side: both screens, CPU and memory charts and every fact that differs.

items.title: Leak finder
items.text: Open a heap dump and see the destroyed Activities and Fragments still alive, the path that keeps each one, and what keeps the most memory.

items.title: Start time and energy
items.text: Cold, warm and hot start times with the median of several runs, and the energy an app used while you used it.

items.title: Budgets and baselines
items.text: Write limits in emulabzip.toml and fail a CI run that breaks them, or that got slower than the last good run.

items.title: Inside Flutter and React Native
items.text: The widget tree, frame times and memory of Flutter apps, and the React tree and Hermes heap of React Native apps, read through their own debuggers.

items.title: GraphQL and gRPC
items.text: Operations and calls named in the request list, queries with their variables, gRPC status and streaming, and protobuf read with or without your .proto files.

items.title: Send again and slow networks
items.text: Resend a request with changes, or make the network slow, laggy, lossy or offline to see how the app copes.

items.title: Timeline, video and replay
items.text: Touches, requests, log problems, slow frames and crashes on one time axis with the screen recording beside it, and a recording of the network that answers your app offline.

items.title: App state as data
items.text: Save an app's data to one file and restore it, see what a migration changed, edit rows and preferences with Undo, make and snapshot emulators, and read Redux, React Query and Realm.

why.title: Built to be trusted with your devices
why.lead: A small, fast and honest tool, made in the open.

items.title: Open source, MIT
items.text: Read the code, run it, change it. No account, no telemetry, no connections of its own.

items.title: Public interfaces only
items.text: ADB, simctl, Perfetto and the accessibility tree. No private frameworks and no agent installed on the device.

items.title: Android and iOS together
items.text: One tool and one habit for both platforms, instead of one tool for each.

items.title: Native and light
items.text: A Rust core with a Tauri interface: a small download, a fast start and low memory use.

items.title: Undoes what it changes
items.text: Proxy settings and device overrides are put back when you stop, also after an error.

items.title: Made to be scripted
items.text: Every feature is in the command line and in the MCP server, with JSON output.

items.a: EmuLabZip is a free, open-source desktop app and command line tool that lets you inspect, monitor and debug apps running in Android emulators and iOS simulators: logs, network traffic, performance, memory, storage, crashes, layout and accessibility.
Yes. EmuLabZip is open source under the MIT license. There is no account, no paid plan and no telemetry.

items.q: Which operating systems does it run on?
items.a: macOS, Windows and Linux. iOS simulators need a Mac with Xcode, because Apple only provides them there. Android emulators work on all three systems.

items.q: Do I need to install anything on the emulator?
items.a: No. EmuLabZip uses the public tools of each platform (ADB and simctl), so nothing is installed on the device or inside your app.

items.q: Can it see my app's HTTPS traffic?
items.a: Yes. The built-in proxy decrypts HTTPS once the emulator trusts the EmuLabZip certificate, which the app installs for you. Apps that pin their certificate are passed through unchanged.

items.q: Does it work with AI assistants?
items.a: Yes. EmuLabZip includes an MCP server, so assistants such as Claude can read logs and crashes, take screenshots, audit accessibility and control the device.

items.q: Can I use it in CI?
items.a: Yes. The emulabzip ci command records a session around your test command, keeps its exit code, and can fail the run when the app crashes or the screen has accessibility problems.
Not yet. Android emulators and iOS simulators are supported today. Physical iPhones and Android over Wi-Fi are planned for v0.15.

final.title: Start debugging your emulators in a minute
final.text: Download the app, boot an emulator or a simulator, and it shows up on its own.
